subject: Decision Making
title: Neurotech and Brain-Computer Interfaces
description: A 60-second lesson on Neurotech and Brain-Computer Interfaces.

hook.text: Neuralink implanted a chip in a human brain. The patient moved a cursor with thought alone.

buildup.text: Brain-computer interfaces, or BCIs, read neural signals and translate them into actions.

discovery.text: As BCIs advance, they could detect decision states before conscious awareness.

twist.text: Neuroscience already showed that brain signals predict decisions 7 seconds before people report being aware of choosing.

climax.text: If machines can read decisions before you are aware of them, who is deciding?

punchline.text: Your brain decides 7 seconds before you know. BCIs can read that signal now.

quiz.question: What ethical question do brain-computer interfaces raise?
options: If machines read decisions before conscious awareness, what does that mean for free will
